To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the robot's motion is determined by the gradient field of the potential function and not by the potential function itself; (2) the potential function must be a smooth function of the robot's position; (3) the potential function is a function of the environment, which is not known a priori; (4) the potential field principle does not guarantee that the robot will reach a goal position, nor does it guarantee that the robot's motion will be smooth; and (5)

the potential field principle can be applied to mobile robot navigation, provided that the following conditions are satisfied: the robot must be a point mass; the environment is static; the robot must move at a constant velocity and at a constant direction; there must be no obstacles in the environment; and the potential field function must have a single minimum.
potential field methods are not suitable for mobile robots that are required to navigate through cluttered, dynamic and/or unstructured environments.
